The assistant described type 2 diabetes mellitus as a chronic metabolic disorder in which insulin resistance or inadequate insulin production impairs blood-sugar regulation. The assistant listed possible symptoms as excessive thirst and urination, increased hunger, fatigue, blurred vision, and slow wound healing or infections. It described management as lifestyle changes, medication, and sometimes insulin therapy; listed metformin, sulfonylureas, DPP-4 inhibitors, GLP-1 agonists, and SGLT2 inhibitors as medication classes; and advised working with healthcare providers and regularly monitoring blood sugar.

records.text: The assistant summarized the paper as reviewing 36 studies published in English from January 2000 through August 2018. It reported a moderate negative relationship between work engagement and workaholism, consistent across samples, countries, industries, and measures, and described the two as distinct but negatively related constructs. The assistant said the authors suggested that promoting work engagement might help prevent or reduce workaholism, which is associated with burnout and impaired well-being.

records.text: In describing the paper’s methods, the assistant said the authors searched PsycINFO, Scopus, and Web of Science for English-language studies published from January 2000 through August 2018; applied inclusion and exclusion criteria requiring data on both work engagement and workaholism; assessed study quality with the Quality Assessment Tool for Quantitative Studies; and pooled effect sizes as correlation coefficients using a random-effects model.
